evals.prompt: Northwind renews in February and their new CFO wants to know what they got for $180k this year. I've got a ticket export and a usage CSV — the ticket one has two title rows above the header and the cost column is text with dollar signs in it.
evals.expected_output: A Measure-mode value case: files ingested without a re-export being requested, benefit lines by class with the arithmetic shown, attribution stated with its level and setter, the conservative scenario as the headline with a sensitivity sentence and a break-even, a cost side that includes the customer's own labour, a coverage ledger over the seven families with a defensibility band, an Assumptions table, and a customer-facing one-pager in a fenced text block below the divider.
assertions: Runs the shared ingest step on the supplied files rather than asking the user to re-export or reformat them, finds the header row beneath the title rows, parses the dollar-signed text column as money, and confirms any column mapping below 0.80 confidence before using it
Asks for and prints the data as-of date rather than treating the export as current
Names the baseline rung (B1-B4) or the counterfactual design (D1-D5) on every benefit line, with its caveat, and never presents an industry proxy as a measurement
States attribution as a factor with its level (A1-A4) and who set it, never 1.0 on a non-cash line, and reports gross alongside attributed movement
Presents the conservative scenario as the headline with central and stretch beside it, plus a break-even and a sensitivity sentence written for the customer artifact
Includes the customer's internal labour, services and training in the cost side, not just the subscription fees
Ends with a Coverage Ledger over all seven families, a defensibility band no higher than the weakest input permits, and an Assumptions table with a concrete consequence per row

Emits the customer-facing one-pager inside a fenced text block below the divider, in the customer's currency and fiscal calendar, containing no health score, risk band, ARR-at-risk, cost-to-serve or commercial ask

evals.prompt: We just closed Meridian Health and kickoff is next week. What should I be doing about ROI?
evals.expected_output: An Establish-mode run: the impact hypothesis form for one to three objectives, a baseline capture plan with a named customer owner and a date inside week one, the KPI instrumentation requirements, and the measurement date set 90 days before the opt-out deadline. No dollar figure yet, and the reason stated.
assertions: Selects Establish mode from the account start date rather than asking which mode to run
Produces impact hypotheses in the six-slot form — named team, metric, baseline, target, measurement system, named customer verifier — and refuses any hypothesis missing a slot
Makes baseline capture a week-one milestone with a named customer owner and a date, and states plainly that the pre-period becomes unrecoverable once the product is live
Limits the scorecard to one to three KPIs, each measurable in a named system with a re-runnable query rather than a survey
Sets the measurement date 90 days before the opt-out deadline (renewal_date minus notice_period_days), not the renewal date
States no dollar figure at this stage and says why, rather than modelling a projected ROI as if it were delivered value

evals.prompt: Their QBR is in three weeks and we never captured a baseline. Can you still build me an ROI number?
evals.expected_output: A Recover-mode run: the recovery ladder worked in order, the highest available rung or design named, a defensibility band capped accordingly, unit metrics rather than a fabricated dollar figure where nothing is available, and a named ask with an owner and a date that fixes the gap for next year.
assertions: Degrades rather than refusing — works the recovery ladder in order and states which rung or design it landed on
Does not fill the gap with an industry benchmark, and never presents a proxy as a measurement
Caps the defensibility band to what the weakest input permits and says which input caps it
Where no dollar figure is defensible, reports unit metrics instead and states plainly that no dollar figure is being given
Gives a named ask with an owner and a date to establish the baseline, and schedules the quarterly refresh
Records every default it ran on in the Assumptions table with a concrete consequence, not 'may affect results'

evals.prompt: Finance is pushing back on the $2.6M value number we gave Acme. They want to know where it came from.
evals.expected_output: A Defend-mode run: the input register with a source and an attester per input, the attribution register with levels and confounders, the sensitivity table with three scenarios and a break-even, the exclusions list, and an honest reduction of any line that cannot be defended.
assertions: Leads with the input register — one source and one named attester per input — and marks anything unsourced as UNKNOWN rather than defending it
Prints the attribution register with the level (A1-A4), the setter and the named confounders for each benefit line
Reduces or removes any line whose attribution is correlation-only, rather than restating the original figure
Presents three scenarios plus the break-even, with the conservative figure as the number being defended
Includes a specific 'not counted in this figure' list rather than a generic disclaimer
Rounds the composite headline to two significant figures and states no probability without a cited backtest
Names no customer-success-platform vendor anywhere, referring to the category generically when it needs to point at where a number lives
